newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Grenade blast in Ethiopian post office wounds two.
newsitem.headline: Grenade blast in Ethiopian post office wounds two.

text.p: A grenade blast in a post office building in the eastern Ethiopian city of Harar wounded two Ethiopians, the state Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) said on Friday.

It said windows of the post office building, where Harar's radio station also has its offices, were shattered by the explosion on Thursday night. A post office guard and a woman working at the radio station were treated at a hospital and later released
British, French and German tourists were wounded in February when a grenade was lobbed into a hotel in the ancient walled city.
Eleven people were wounded when a bomb explosion ripped through a bar in the eastern railway town of Dire Dawa in April.
The Dire Dawa attack followed three hand grenade blasts in the capital Addis Ababa earlier in April that killed one person and wounded 75, including four Britons and a French couple.
The Ethiopian government blamed Moslem fundamentalists for several bomb attacks last year but no claims of responsibility were made for those explosions or the similar attacks this year.
